To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the effect of GVS on egocentric mental transformation is specific to right anodal G VS and to egocentric mental rotation.
the effect of GVS on mental transformation tasks may be modulated by the type of task, the type of stimulus, and the type of imagined motion.
right but not left galvanic vestibulostimulation increases response time during mental transformations of the roll plane.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the influence of the vestibular system on the processing of mental imagery and spatial transformations.
the influence of vestibular processing on mental transformations.
the influence of GVS on the mental transformation of body and objects.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the influence of vestibular stimulation on object-based and egocentric mental transformation is complex and depends on the task and the subject.
the effect of right anodeal GVS depends on the type of mental transformation and the individual strategy of mental rotation.
right anodal GSV interferes more with the egocentric than with the object-based transformation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the vestibular system is involved in the control of mental imagery of spatial transformations.
right anodal GSV interferes with the processing of mental transformations, especially when they involve an egocentric frame of reference.
GVS can influence mental imagery and that the influence of GVS depends on the type of mental transformation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the vestibular system may play an important role in the processing of mental transformations.
vestibular stimulation can interfere with mental transformations in the same way as other forms of mental rotation.
GVS can modulate mental transformations and that the effect depends on the type of transformation (egocentric vs object-based).
